abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) worldwide, but site-specific N-glycosylation signatures associated with renal injury in DKD remain poorly characterized. Unlike previous studies relying on suboptimal control tissues, we utilized intact healthy kidney donor (HKD) cortical biopsies as physiologically relevant reference tissues. We applied an optimized quantitative glycoproteomic pipeline combining homogenization and noncontact ultrasound-assisted protein extraction, ZIC-HILIC enrichment, and EThcD-sceHCD-MS/MS to profile intact N-glycopeptides (IGPs) from 20 DKD patients and 20 HKD controls. We identified 1186 significantly differentially expressed IGPs and 111 altered N-glycans derived from 294 glycoproteins in DKD renal tissues (adjusted p value of <0.05, FC of >1.5 or <0.67). GO enrichment and KEGG pathway analyses revealed the enrichment of differentially glycosylated proteins in the complement and coagulation cascades and immune-related glycoproteins. Hybrid, complex, fucosylated, and sialylated N-glycans were more frequently represented among upregulated in DKD, whereas high-mannose structures were more frequently represented among downregulated IGP. Subclass- and site-specific N-glycosylation profiling of IgGs, IgA2, and complement proteins uncovered unique DKD-associated glycosomal alterations. This study identifies novel DKD glyco-signatures from immunoglobulins and complement components, demonstrates the feasibility of our workflow for limited clinical biopsy material, and offers mechanistic insights alongside candidate molecular signatures for future validation.
